attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated as his account of events.

semantics.note: Faithful: a contemporaneous observation of a reported GPU purchase for an undisclosed generative AI project, with Twitter's revenue and credibility in decline at the same time. 'While' is a qualifier, not a conditional. The approximate count is preserved as the threshold.

contract.note: The readings of the purchase, the mystery and credibility are ordinary. Narrowing 'revenue burns' to March 2023 total revenue is an evaluator choice; the speaker named no period. That choice decides the result, because the packet has no March figure. The reading is still a plausible one, not stretched against the speaker.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous report, citing Business Insider, of about 10,000 GPUs for a Twitter AI/LLM project with no stated end goal. Not independent of e2.
Contemporaneous report of roughly 10,000 GPUs for a generative AI project whose nature was 'still a mystery'. Same underlying source as e1.
WBUR's direct statement that it was leaving Twitter over Musk's actions. This documents institutional loss of confidence within the target period.
Top-ten advertiser spending over an undefined two-month window, plus Musk's own claim of a 50% decline. Neither is March total revenue on a comparable basis.
Musk's claim that advertisers were returning is a self-interested company statement. The 40% revenue decline it reports is for December, a different period. Neither settles March revenue.

reviews.rationale: The GPU purchase, its undisclosed generative AI use (e1, e2) and the institutional credibility loss (e3) are supported. The contract also requires a decline in March 2023 total revenue. The packet has only selected-advertiser estimates, Musk's own statements and a December figure, all context. The revenue condition is unsettled, so the full support condition is not met.
